name: Monster Trainer Monslinger
body:
Monslingers are monster trainers who utilize firearms when calling on their companion monsters. By bonding with their firearm of choice, these trainers can “load” their essence into the weapon. Upon firing it, their monster is called for one round, casting one of its trainer spells as determined by the trainer, then returning to the trainer’s essence to recharge.

When used in this way, monsters don’t typically grow like they do under the care of a traditional monster trainer. Instead, outside of being fired from the monslinger’s weapon, they remain in their earliest known form, and only specialized firearms are capable of allowing them to grow to their higher stages. The tradeoff is that a monslinger with a powerful enough weapon can use her monsters to cast lower-level spells almost indefinitely, so long as she manages her flare.

Saving Throws

A monslinger’s Will save is poor and progresses at the same rate as her Fortitude saving throws (1/3 of her monster trainer level).

This alters the monster trainer’s Will save progression.

Weapon Proficiencies

Monslingers are proficient with all simple weapons and all firearms.

This alters the monster trainer’s weapon proficiencies.

Gunsmith

At 1st level, a monslinger gains one of the following weapons of her choice: any crossbow, blunderbuss, musket, or pistol. Her starting weapon is battered, and only she knows how to use it properly. All other creatures treat her gun as if it had the broken condition. If the weapon already has the broken condition, it does not work at all for anyone else trying to use it. This starting weapon can only be sold for scrap (it’s worth 4d10 gp when sold).

If her starting weapon is a crossbow, the weapon is treated as masterwork when she wields it.

If her starting weapon is a firearm, the monslinger also gains Gunsmithing as a bonus feat.

Once she has a masterwork weapon, the monslinger can enchant it for half the price, as if she crafted it herself, but it still only functions for her.

Flare (Ex)

Flare is a measure of the monslinger’s essence and her ability to exert it when firing monsters from her weapon of choice. Except as noted here, this functions identically to the gunslinger’s grit class feature. Monslingers can take the Extra Grit feat to increase their maximum flare and gain additional flare at the start of each day.

At the start of each day, the monslinger can assign an amount of flare to her monsters equal to her Charisma modifier. The flare is divided between her monsters, so the monslinger must choose carefully which she wants available to use initially, and she spends flare each time she fires her weapon to call upon a monster.

This ability replaces spell familiarity.

Monslinging (Sp)

When a monslinger uses her weapon to launch a monster at her enemies, it’s referred to as monslinging. Monslinging has two base effects that the monslinger can use: Monster strike and cast a spell.

This ability replaces spellcasting and trainer perks.

Monster Strike: As long as her monster has at least 1 flare remaining, the monslinger can call upon it by making an attack roll against a target within range of her weapon. If the target is within 1 range increment, the monslinger targets its touch AC instead. Alternatively, the monslinger can spend 1 flare when she makes her first attack each round to automatically hit (but not critically hit) targets with her initial attack rolls until the start of her next turn. If she does, targets still receive the benefits of any miss chance, cover, or concealment they may have.

If the monslinger’s initial attack hits, her monster becomes the weapon’s ammunition, travels to the target, and makes a single attack against it, adding the weapon’s damage to its own before determining immunities, resistances, and weaknesses. If either attack is a confirmed critical hit, all damage is multiplied by whichever critical multiplier is higher. Because the initial attack considers cover, concealment, or miss chance, the monster’s attack is treated as having already bypassed it.

Weapon qualities such as scatter still function when the monslinger fires her weapon, but they do not add the monster’s attack, damage, or other abilities against any targets beyond the initial one, nor can she hit additional targets automatically (unless another ability allows her to do so).

Cast a Spell: By spending 1 flare, a monslinger can fire her weapon, calling upon her monster, which casts a 1st- or 2nd-level spell on its trainer list (0-level spells can still be cast by the monster at will without spending flare or being fired from the monslinger’s weapon). The monslinger must have access to spells of the appropriate level before her monsters can cast them in this way.

As she and her monsters gain experience, the monslinger can use more flare to cast higher-level spells with the monsters she launches from her weapon. It costs 4 flare to cast a 5th-level or lower spell, 7 flare to cast an 8th-level or lower spell, and 9 flare to cast a 9th-level spell. The monslinger can bring these costs down in a number of ways, but the primary method is to reduce them by an amount of flare equal to her weapon’s enhancement bonus (up to +5). This cannot reduce the cost to cast a spell below 1 flare, and a monster must still be granted that amount of flare at least once in the day before it can cast such spells.

For example, before her bovinae gains the ability to cast crashing rocks, Solisa must assign it a total of 9 flare at some point during the day. She can assign it 3 flare at the start of the day, and the other 6 as she gains it, even if she spends some while adventuring to cast other spells or make more accurate attacks. Once the bovinae reaches its threshold, it only costs Solisa 4 flare to cast that spell from her +5 pistol.

Unlike monster strike, casting a spell with her firearm has no effect on the spell itself. Without metamagic feats or other abilities, the spell still has the same range, costly materials (if any), and all other aspects as normal. The firearm’s range increment does not penalize the monslinger when casting a spell, nor do any of its weapon qualities (such as scatter) modify the spell.

Monster Growth

At 2nd level, and every level thereafter, the monslinger begins each day with 1 additional flare she can grant to a monster capable of growing at that level. If a monster is capable of growing twice at her current level, the monslinger can grant it up to 2 additional flare total. Monsters that grow beginning at 2nd level include hippogriffs and most lagomorphs, which are some of the most frequently captured and used early monsters.

As long as it has at least 1 flare remaining when the monslinger calls upon it, a monster can grow as part of being launched from her weapon, allowing it to make more powerful strikes or cast more potent spells. A monster reduces the cost to cast its spells by 1 when it grows to its second stage or higher, and by 2 when it reaches its final stage of growth, to a minimum of 1 flare.

Utility Flare (Ex)

At 3rd level, a monslinger can select utility flare in place of talented trainer. Utility flare allows her to call upon her monster to cast a beneficial, non-damaging spell on her or her allies and spend 1 fewer flare to do so. If this would reduce the flare spent to 0, the monster can cast that spell as long as it has at least 1 flare remaining. At 9th level, she gains the option she didn’t choose at 3rd.

This ability alters talented trainer and replaces great trainer.
